conditionTones.idle: Faint Ink dot, Muted Ink text, Strong Hairline edge: not recording.
conditionTones.calm: Working Violet dot, Lavender text, violet edge at 0.6: recording and reaching the server; the dot breathes.
conditionTones.attention: Attention Amber dot, text and edge at 0.6: offline, stale GPS, paused or delayed trip, uploads waiting, storage failing, permission denied while recording.
conditionTones.alert: Alarm Red dot and edge on rgb(48 14 22 / 0.92): SOS countdown, sending, queued or active; check-in requested. Alert outranks attention, attention outranks calm.

extensions.motionBudget: The tracker moves only to carry state (sheet, tone, recording dot, marker ping, live SOS); no ambient background motion. Ambient motion lives on the landing and sign-in pages.

What Safe Location will never do: ruled two-column list

narrative.overview:
Safe Location is a map at night with an instrument laid over it. The map fills the screen and shows where you have been; the instrument answers "am I being recorded, and is it reaching anyone?" in two places that never scroll away: a floating status pill that carries the overall tone in one short line, and the top of the sheet, where a large state line, the next-reading countdown, an event message and the main actions sit. Readings, trip, history and settings live further down the same sheet at lower weight. SOS floats on the map in thumb reach, red and round, with Call 112 above it.

Density is moderate and calm. The sheet is one charcoal-violet surface divided by hairline rules rather than a stack of floating cards; colour is almost entirely neutral until something needs a person's attention, and then it appears in exactly one place, with one meaning. The face is Geist, self-hosted and small (29 KB for Latin), so the product reads like a modern SaaS tool without a font service; text shows at once in the system font and swaps when Geist arrives. The tracker's ground is now the dark map itself, tinted violet-black; the signal field (violet light from above, pink corner glow, point grid, grain) remains the ground of the account, sign-in and landing pages.

Motion follows a budget. The tracker stays open for hours on a phone battery, so it moves only to say something: the sheet slides, the pill changes tone, the status dot breathes while recording is healthy, the latest-position marker pings, and a hidden active SOS pulses so it is never forgotten. Nothing drifts in the background. Ambient motion lives on the short-visit pages: the sign-in veil breathes, and the public landing page at /welcome (a Persuade-mode page in the same world) drifts an aurora and animates a preview of the real tracker.

The world is honest about uncertainty. Readings show their age and accuracy in tabular numerals, gaps are drawn as dashed lines, doubtful points are amber and left off the route, and nothing in the copy claims a message was delivered unless the provider confirmed it. The landing page's previews only show states the product really shows.
keyCharacteristics: Map first: a full-screen dark map on phones, a 400px panel beside the map on computers.
One tone-carrying status pill per screen, driven by state (idle grey, calm violet, attention amber, alert red).
One sheet of hairline-ruled sections instead of card stacks; peek, half and full heights on phones.
Violet means working, amber means attention, red means emergency, failure or irreversible removal.
Geist (self-hosted, system fallback), weights 600 to 800, tabular numerals for every reading.
Flat, bordered surfaces inside the sheet; soft shadow only on things that float over the map.
A round red SOS always one tap away, with Call 112 beside it.
Motion budget: tracker motion only to carry state, ambient motion on the landing and sign-in pages, all of it off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Red Means Danger Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for an emergency (SOS, Call 112, alert tone, check-in requested), a failure (denied permission, rejected upload, error) or an irreversible removal (delete, remove, clear, cancel trip). Removal is outline-only red unless it is the confirmed final submit. A merely doubtful reading is amber, never red.

rules.name: The One Meaning Per Hue Rule
rules.body: Violet is working state, amber is attention, green is confirmed fact. A hue never borrows another's meaning, and state is never carried by colour alone: every tone has a sentence or a label. Aurora Pink is light, not a state, so it carries no meaning at all.

rules.name: The Tabular Reading Rule
rules.body: Every number that updates (times, countdowns, accuracy, coordinates, counts) is set with tabular numerals so live readings tick without layout shift. This holds inside the landing previews too.

rules.name: The Light Font Rule
rules.body: One self-hosted family only (Geist), subset by script and loaded with `swap`, so text never waits for a download. No font services, no icon fonts, no second display family.

rules.name: The Status First Rule
rules.body: On every viewport the status pill and the peek sheet's state line and actions are visible without scrolling, and SOS and Call 112 are always one tap away: floating on the map, or pinned at the top of the sheet when it is full.

rules.name: The Map Stays Clear Rule
rules.body: Only the status pill, Recenter, the SOS dock and transient notices float over the map. Everything else lives in the sheet; floating controls step aside when the sheet rises.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Stacked Rule
rules.body: Group related panels as one sheet whose sections are divided by hairlines, and lay readings on a grid whose 1px gaps show the border colour. Do not stack floating, shadowed cards.

rules.name: The Float Only Over The Map Rule
rules.body: Shadow and blur belong to things that float over the map and to overlay cards. Nothing inside the sheet casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Motion Budget Rule
rules.body: The tracker runs for hours on a phone battery, so it moves only to carry state: the sheet sliding (420ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), the pill's tone easing over 400ms, the breathing dot while recording is healthy (2.4s), the latest-marker ping (2.4s), the pulse on a hidden active SOS and the live-SOS dot (1.6s), the countdown ring emptying, overlays fading in (200ms) and rising (320ms). No ambient background motion. Everywhere, `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` stops every animation and transition, and content never depends on motion to be visible.

dos: **Do** let one status pill per screen carry the overall tone, with a short line on screen and the full plain sentence for screen readers.
**Do** keep the state line and the main actions inside the sheet's peek height, and SOS and Call 112 one tap away at every sheet height.
**Do** use Working Violet for working state, Attention Amber for attention, and red only for emergency, failure and irreversible removal.
**Do** keep Aurora Pink as light only: field glows, aurora, rail ends; never a fill, text colour or state.
**Do** set every live reading in tabular numerals at 650 weight, label over value, on a hairline-ruled grid.
**Do** group related sections into one sheet divided by 1px hairlines, and keep everything but the status pill, Recenter and SOS off the map.
**Do** keep primary controls at least 44px tall and keep accessible names when a label is visually hidden.

**Do** honour reduced motion everywhere: stop the sheet slide, tone transitions, breathing dot, marker ping, SOS pulses, overlay entrances, spinner, veil, aurora and previews, and keep content visible without motion or JavaScript.
**Do** make landing previews show only states the product really shows, in the same honest delivery language.
**Do** show age and accuracy with every location and say "simulated" or "submitted" until a provider confirms delivery.
donts: **Don't** use red for a doubtful reading such as a GPS jump or low accuracy; that is amber.
**Don't** add ambient background motion to the tracker; motion there only carries state (sheet, tone, recording, latest position, live SOS). Ambient motion belongs to the landing and sign-in pages.
**Don't** add eyebrows or kickers (small uppercase labels above headings); section titles stand alone in sentence case.
**Don't** stack shadowed, same-weight cards where a ruled sheet will do; shadows belong only to things floating over the map and to overlay cards, and landing glows stay on the landing.
**Don't** put more controls on the map (zoom buttons on phones, layer switchers, extra floating buttons); they go in the sheet.
**Don't** add font services, a second family or icon fonts; use self-hosted Geist and inline SVG icons.
**Don't** claim a message was delivered, or that someone is safe or in danger, without provider confirmation or the person's own action.
**Don't** fabricate streets, routes, accuracy or results to fill an empty state; say what is unknown.
